verdicts.quote: A permitted user can identify and open Grok through signed-in Salesforce Lightning navigation without a separate website, a copied URL, or a separate xAI login.
It does not include Salesforce record fields, IDs, page context, user identity, permission data or Salesforce session material drawn from the org.
The conversation content consists of the submitted text and the bounded prior user and assistant text. It does not include Salesforce record fields
A signed-in Salesforce user is refused before any Grok request if the operator has never granted bot use... Bot administration requires a separate administrative grant.
After a view ends, there is no bot-provided way for a user or administrator to retrieve its draft, prompts, answers or pending outcomes.
A synchronous record-trigger transaction cannot obtain a Grok answer by making an Apex callout inline.
verdicts.missing: The spec states the trigger and uncommitted-DML restrictions (C-77) but never commits to an asynchronous design (Queueable, future, batch); C-133 even contemplates synchronous Apex.
